Theni jailbreak: Human error led to escape of prisoners, says DGP-Prisons Sandeep Rai Rathore; nine guards suspended
 Security audit of all prisons had been ordered after the escape of a prisoner in Puzhal recently
 Updated - October 27, 2026 07:14 pm IST - CHENNAI 
 S. Vijay Kumar READ LATER 
 SEE ALL 
 Remove 
 Sandeep Rai Rathore, DGP, Prisions, after an inspection at the District Prison at Thekkampatti in Theni district, Tamil Nadu, on October 27, 2026
 | Photo Credit: G. Karthikeyan
 A ‘human error’ led to the escape of 17 inmates from the Theni district jail on Monday (October 26, 2026) night, Director-General of Police, Prisons, Sandeep Rai Rathore, said.
 While 13 of the escaped prisoners were already secured, an intensive combing operation was under way in Theni district and adjoining areas to apprehend the others. The State authorities were in touch with their counterpart in Keralam to mount vigil on all roads leading to the inter-State borders. 
 Related Stories
 17 remand prisoners escape from sub-jail in Theni district; 13 held so far 
 Theni jailbreak: Efforts are on to nab escaped prisoners who are still absconding, says T.N. Law Minister Nirmal Kumar 
 The inmates, five of whom were involved in a sensational murder case in Vikramangalam police station limits in Madurai district, overpowered jail warders and escaped through the main entry. 
 “There was a clear breach of security protocol as the prisoners managed to pass through a three-tier barrier manned by security personnel. Some prison staff were carried away by the claim that an inmate had suffered epilepsy and was battling for life. Their focus was on shifting him to the hospital. The prisoners took advantage of this gap and escaped,” Dr. Rathore told The Hindu on Tuesday (October 27). 
 Prison guards suspended 
 Nine prison guards in different ranks were placed under suspension. 
 The DGP said a detailed inquiry had been ordered into the lapses and circumstances that led to the escape of the prisoners, and firm action would be taken against the staff found guilty of dereliction of duty. Parrying questions on the possibility of some prison officials colluding with the accused prisoners, he said any such nexus would be known only after the inquiry.
 Security audit under way
 Dr. Rathore said a security audit of all prisons in Tamil Nadu was ordered soon after the escape of a Nepali prisoner in Puzhal central prison recently. It came to light that the electrified fence had been defunct for quite some time. 
 When 43 LTTE militants escaped from Vellore Fort special camp in 1995 “A gap analysis is under way in all prison complexes across the State. Prisons are hardened targets where foolproof security arrangements should be in place…there should be no room for any complacency,” he said.
 Two Puzhal prison escapees held; 7 staff suspended “Soon after the escape of prisoners was reported, we alerted senior officers in South and Central Zone to conduct vehicle checks and enhance surveillance in railway stations, bus stands, etc. We are working in coordination with the DGP of Keralam in the search operations,” Dr. Aggarwal said.
 #Theni jailbreak: As of Tuesday evening, 13 of the 17 remand prisoners who escaped from Theni district sub-jail at Thekkampatti on October 26 night, have been nabbed by special teams, says DGP-Prisons Sandeep Rai Rathore after visiting the jail.
